question: In the morning a coach had 195 minutes booked for each training session, more than three hours, but cut 154 minutes from every session. She ran 4 sessions that morning. In the afternoon the time from the morning sessions was shared equally among 4 trainees to record on their cards. In the evening one trainee, Kay, noted that she would train exactly the same way on each of 3 days. How many minutes will Kay record for the 3 days?

A single toy warehouse started the morning with 240 dolls in stock. By midmorning, a holiday order left the warehouse with 4 times as many dolls. In the afternoon, 238 dolls were sent to a damaged-goods return. Later that afternoon, a regional contract multiplied that count by 5, and a second contract multiplied it by 6, after a negotiation that took about 120 minutes, right around 2 hours. That evening, 3935 dolls were shipped out to stores, around the time a rival warehouse reported holding 700 dolls, unrelated to this count. Finally, a citywide order multiplied the remaining dolls by 4. How many dolls were in the warehouse by the end of the evening?

A farm shop opened the morning with 73 punnets of strawberries. A grower's van added 41 more punnets before the doors opened. Every punnet on the shelf holds 6 strawberries. A picker dropped off 10 loose strawberries at midday for the tasting bowl. Through the afternoon and evening customers bought 455 strawberries in all. The shop has sold this variety for a dozen summers. How many strawberries are left in the shop?

A farm's water tank holds 224 gallons. The tank is 2 metres tall. The farmer measures water in pints, and since a gallon is 8 pints, he wrote down the tank's contents in pints. He drew off 1285 pints for the cattle, then a rain shower added 73 pints. He drew off another 479 pints for the vegetable beds, and a leaking pipe dripped 3 pints back into the tank. How many pints of water were in the tank?

A parking garage had 158 cars in the morning. In the morning, 91 cars left for work. Later that morning, 62 more cars left for a nearby event. In the afternoon, 31 cars pulled in for a late meeting. That evening, a matching valet service multiplied the remaining cars by 7, around the time a second garage across town charged 8 dollars an hour, unrelated to this count. How many cars were in the garage by the end of the evening?

Rosa had 225 cookies. Her friend Emma had 300 cookies. Rosa baked 79 more cookies. Then 207 were bought for a party. She returned 87 burned ones. She multiplied her remaining stock by 8 for a catering order. How many cookies does Rosa have?

A workshop had 189 pieces. They multiplied by 9 for expanded production. They subtracted 70 pieces completed. They subtracted 7 more pieces damaged. Finally, 174 pieces were removed for quality. Using minutes and hours conversion, and tracking the intermediate quantity state, how many pieces remain?

Nina had 82 dollars saved, even though her piggy bank has a dozen coin slots. She spent 59 dollars on a new backpack, out of the 20 styles the store carried. She then paid 9 dollars for a bus pass. A birthday gift from three relatives, each matching her remaining amount, made her total four times as large. Finally, she earned 7 more dollars from selling lemonade, ending up with more than her cousin Ella, who only had 30 dollars. How much money did Nina have at the end?

A stadium's ticket count starts at 175 season passes sold, in a venue that has stood for half a century, unrelated to today's sales. A bulk corporate order multiplies the passes by 8. Then 77 more passes are sold at the box office. A partner promotion multiplies the total by 5. Afterward, 4634 passes are transferred to a sister stadium for a shared event. Finally, 52 more passes are sold as walk-up sales. How many season passes does the original stadium have on record now?

On Monday morning a flooring firm had 134 boxes of underlay stacked in the yard, and a lorry brought 31 more before lunch. In the afternoon the fitters checked the stack and found that every box holds 4 packs. In the early evening they opened the packs and found 2 rolls inside each pack, and every roll measures 3 metres. The firm's van was serviced 5 weeks ago. How many metres of underlay does the firm have in the yard?

A business had 90 dollars. They divided by 5 to create service tiers. They added 5 dollars. They added 72 more (afternoon). They added 65 additional (evening). They subtracted 61 for expenses. Tom's account had 200 dollars separately (named comparison). Using 'minutes to hours'—after division and initial addition but before afternoon additions, how much money?

A charity jar held 20 dollars in donations at the start of the fundraiser morning. By midday, the treasurer split the jar evenly between 2 charity boxes and kept tracking only one box, ignoring the 200 raffle tickets that had gone unsold. In the afternoon, a generous donor added 73 dollars to that box. That evening, a matching-donation program grew the box's total to 5 times its size. Overnight, processing fees shrank it back down to one-fifth of that amount by morning, and since 100 cents make 1 dollar, the bank always rounded exactly to the cent. Finally, 82 dollars had to be paid out the next day for venue costs. How much money was left in the box?

A shop started with 151 items. They received 25 more items. Their inventory increased 6 times. They got 7 more items. Finally, they added 47 more items. Her father had 80 items. How many items does the shop have at the end?

In a trivia tournament, Hana's team started the final day with 238 points on the scoreboard. In the morning quiz they earned 22 points, and in the lunchtime quiz they earned 31 more. A penalty for a late answer then cost them 218 points, and a second penalty cost them 35 points, which put Hana's team behind Leo's team for the first time all day. In the lightning round every point on Hana's team's scoreboard was worth 8 points, and after that a bonus question added 13 points. How many points did Hana's team have on the scoreboard at the end of the day?

Two managers, Jordan and Liu, reviewed a quarterly report. They started with 212 items in stock. Jordan multiplied the count by 5 for planning. Then 35 items were added. The quarterly loss was 618 items to breakage. Another 167 items were recalled. Everything was doubled for next quarter's forecast. Then it was tripled again for contingency. How many items are in the contingency forecast?

A student had 139 problems to solve. He added 3. This was doubled. He added 41. He removed 58 already solved. This was multiplied by 5. Then multiplied by 8. A bonus section had 27 problems. How many total?

A bookstore had 225 copies of a bestselling novel in its warehouse. A reprint order doubled the warehouse's stock. A small delivery added 34 more copies. A big chain order then took 364 copies out of the warehouse. The remaining copies were split evenly among 5 branch stores, and only the flagship branch's share was tracked from then on. A separate warehouse across town, unrelated to this stock, held 900 copies of a different book. Finally, a return shipment added 45 more copies to the flagship branch's tracked share. How many copies were in the flagship branch's tracked share?
A work schedule had 61 units. Multiplied by 6. By 2. Divided by 6. Added 77. Removed 118 for breaks. What is work time?
A chef had 185 portions. He multiplied by 5. He added 41 more. He divided by 3. He multiplied by 8. How many portions?

A store manager began with 60 items. They subtracted 52 from morning sales. They added 27 from restocking. They subtracted 14 from damage. They subtracted 3 more from shrinkage (measured in final inventory items). Throughout the day, morning opening, afternoon customers, and evening closeout tracked movement. What was the final inventory count?

On Monday morning a bike courier set off with 135 envelopes and delivered 39 of them before ten o'clock. Before lunch a further 71 were dropped off on the second run. In the afternoon he found that every envelope still in his bag holds 7 documents. In the evening 34 of those documents were pulled out as duplicates, and each document that was left had to be stamped 4 times. How many stamps did the courier make?

A contractor started with 153 tasks. They added 37 tasks, multiplied total by 5 for crew assignment, lost 453 to scope reduction, and multiplied by 3 for deadline acceleration. What is the accelerated task count?

Two delivery drivers, Jake and Sofia, track packages. Sofia started with 82 packages. She added 16 from a pickup. Then added 67 more. This total was multiplied by 9 for route organization. This was divided by 3 for equal stops. Then 351 were delivered. The remainder was multiplied by 7. By time of delivery (hours), what was Sofia's final count?

A collection starts with 185 items. They lose 1 item to removal. They add 17 items from acquisition. They add 18 items from donation. They lose 7 items to discarding. They lose 53 items to redistribution. Converting to dozens, how many items remain?

Ruth organises more races than her co-organiser Emeka does. The medal box held 202 medals before the marathon, and half of them were given out at the finish line. A sponsor then sent 61 new medals for the box. A club returned 9 medals that had been engraved wrongly, and the engraver delivered 29 more. A school finally donated 71 spare medals to the same box. How many medals are in the box now?
